sections.label: System
sections.info: Configure region / base hardware selection / ROM mapping / Sega CD RAM cart.

items.label: System Region
items.info: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL'/'Europe' is 50hz while 'NTSC'/'US' is 60hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal (or produce errors) if the incorrect region is selected.

items.label: Master System Type
items.info: Choose which type of hardware (SMS or Game Gear) the core should emulate when running Master System content.

items.label: Master System ROM Mapping
items.info: Choose which ROM mapper the core should apply. 'Auto' will work for a wide range of content, but in some cases automatic detection fails.

items.label: Master System Palette in TMS modes
items.info: Choose which colour palette should be used when an SMS game runs in one of the SG-1000 graphics modes.

items.label: Sega CD RAM Cart
items.info: Emulate a Sega CD RAM cart, used for save game data. WARNING: When enabled, internal save data (BRAM) will be discarded.

sections.label: Video
sections.info: Configure aspect ratio / LCD filter / video renderer.

items.label: Core-Provided Aspect Ratio
items.info: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core Provided' in the Video settings.

items.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
items.info: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and 'Genesis Nomad' LCD panels.

items.label: Video Renderer
items.info: Specify video rendering method. 'Accurate' is slowest, but most exact. 'Good' is faster, but fails if colors change mid-frame too often. 'Fast' renders the complete frame in one pass, and is incompatible with games that rely on mid-frame palette/sprite table updates.

sections.label: Audio
sections.info: Configure sample rate / emulated audio devices / low pass filter / FM chip type.

items.label: Audio Sample Rate (Hz)
items.info: Higher values increase sound quality. Lower values may increase performance. Native is the Mega Drive sound chip rate (~53000). Select this if you want the most accurate audio.

items.label: FM filtering
items.info: Enable filtering for Mega Drive FM sound at non-native bitrates. Sound output will improve, at the price of being noticeably slower

items.label: Master System FM Sound Unit
items.info: Enable emulation of the SMS FM Sound Unit. This produces higher quality audio in some games, but non-Japanese titles may fail to run.

items.label: Mega Drive FM chip type
items.info: Select the Mega Drive/Genesis FM chip type. Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis mostly used YM2612, which produced a distinct distortion. YM3438 was used in model 2 consoles.

items.label: Audio Filter
items.info: Enable a low pass audio filter to better simulate the characteristic sound of a Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. Note that only Model 1 and its add-ons (Sega CD, 32X) employed a physical low pass filter.

items.label: Low-Pass Filter %
items.info: Specify the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

items.label: Mouse Speed
items.info: Select the mouse sensivity. This setting is used by both the Sega Mouse and the Pico Pen. Higher values increase the mouse speed.

items.label: Dynamic Recompilers
items.info: Enable dynamic recompilers which help to improve performance. Less accurate than interpreter CPU cores, but significantly faster.

items.label: Frameskip
items.info: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

items.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
items.info: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

sections.label: Emulation Hacks
sections.info: Configure sprite limit removal / processor overclocking.

items.label: No Sprite Limit
items.info: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

items.label: 68K Overclock
items.info: Overclock the emulated 68K chip. Can reduce slowdown, but may cause glitches.
